advice: Experiment: in the n=512 assembly, change the scratch layout used by `Llibxsmm_78` and consumed by `Llibxsmm_478`/`Llibxsmm_70c`. The A-transpose scratch currently uses 512 FP32 values per K row (2048 bytes), and the K loop advances its x3 stream by 256 bytes. Test a 513-float row stride: allocate enough stack space for 512 such rows, store each transposed row at `row*513`, and update the x3 K-step and panel-rewind arithmetic to use the padded stride. The extra element per row shifts successive row starts by four bytes, which may alter cache-set mapping for the scratch stream. Hypothesis: this may reduce harmful cache conflicts; the supplied cache capacities do not establish that conflicts occur. Measure the full stack allocation, packing, and kernel traffic inside `gemm`; retain the same tile traversal and arithmetic.
risks: The existing 128 KiB scratch allocation exactly holds 512×512 floats, so padding needs 2,048 additional bytes and corrected stack reservation/alignment. Every pack destination and x3 advance/rewind must use the new stride without overlap, out-of-bounds access, or changing which values the paired loads consume. The changed stride can also worsen locality or add address work. Keep the general-size fallback, ABI, FP32 accumulation, flags, and tolerance unchanged. Check assembly legality and stack bounds, then correctness for n=512 and general odd/tail sizes plus n<=0. Compare repeated scores with fresh paired unchanged controls on the same power source and settings, report spread, and do not infer cache-conflict causality from noisy scores or attribute a joint result to this proposal.
